recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-10399 unless FHIR-I separately reopens DELETE success response-code guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-10399 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request for the FHIR-core HTTP page. It reported that the delete interaction appeared to allow 200 OK only when a resource was already deleted, while successful deletion or a nonexistent resource appeared to allow only 204 No Content.
initial_application: No git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-10399. The Jira comment says it was already fixed under a different task; the matching task is FHIR-12216/#12216, applied by git-svn commit 3d7763fc7d0a1a1921562cf73de46c53197d669e for svn @10126, which changed both DELETE sentences to the current 200 OK with payload / 204 No Content without payload wording.
additional_context: source/http.html is the active HTTP page via publish.ini [pages]. The combined branch already contains a no-change audit commit for FHIR-12216, so that related issue was not republished. Direct FHIR-10399 Zulip and Confluence searches found no hits, and broader DELETE 200/204 Zulip discussion did not overturn the applied rule.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Current source/http.html already says successful or nonexistent deletes and already-deleted deletes return either 200 OK if the response contains a payload or 204 No Content with no response payload.

related_jiras.note: Published/Persuasive issue that applied the same DELETE response-code alignment and is already represented on the combined branch.
